findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and inviting brute-force and exploitation attempts.
Inbound TCP/80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and only plaintext HTTP is served, so traffic to the portal is unencrypted in transit and the port is globally reachable.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel from the instance.

AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the instance user_data script; user data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute and is stored in version control.
No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so the instance permits unauthenticated IMDSv1 credential retrieval, turning any SSRF in the web app into credential theft.

The instance is launched in a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and routed directly to an internet gateway, giving it a public address and direct internet exposure with no private network layer.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance root EBS volume may be created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so data stored on the attached disk is unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume and is therefore unencrypted, and snapshots are easily shared/copied across accounts, spreading unprotected data.
The VPC flow log archive bucket has no server-side encryption configuration (no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), so sensitive network telemetry is stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or ACL/policy restriction is defined for the flow log bucket, leaving it without an explicit guardrail against public or cross-account exposure of network logs.
The audit-log destination bucket has no versioning or MFA-delete/object-lock protection and sets force_destroy = true, so flow log evidence can be deleted or overwritten without trace.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, removing the private network layer and exposing workloads directly to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, removing the private network layer and exposing workloads directly to the internet.

The VPC is created without an accompanying aws_default_security_group resource restricting all rules, so the default security group remains with its permissive default rules for any resource that lands in it.
